headline: Record adjusted profit despite near-flat headline sales

kpis.label: Net cash used in operating activities

summary_short: Smithfield Foods' Q1 FY2026 sales grew 0.8% y/y to $3.80B while adjusted operating profit hit a first-quarter record of $339M (+4.0%) and adjusted diluted EPS rose to $0.64 (+10.3%); net income attributable to Smithfield rose 10.0% to $246M ($0.62 diluted EPS).
summary_long: Q1 FY2026 sales rose 0.8% y/y to $3.80B: Packaged Meats gained 6.2% on Easter-timing volume and cost-driven pricing, while Hog Production fell 17.5% against a one-time 2025 hog-inventory sale. Operating margin rose 22bps to 8.7% (adjusted 8.9%, up from 8.6%) as SG&A fell 8.6%. Net income rose 10.0% to $246M ($0.62 diluted EPS); adjusted diluted EPS rose 10.3% to $0.64 and adjusted EBITDA rose 5.3% to $417M, a first-quarter record. Operating cash outflow narrowed to $65M from $166M. Cash was $1.39B; net debt/adjusted EBITDA was 0.4x. Reaffirming FY2026 guidance (adjusted operating profit $1,325-1,475M, capex $350-450M, tax rate 22.5%-24.5%), excluding the pending Nathan's Famous acquisition (~$450-500M cash, expected H2 2026 close).

drivers.explanation: Packaged Meats sales +$125M (+6.2%) on Easter-timing volume gains and pricing that passed through higher raw-material costs, largely offset by Hog Production sales -$163M (-17.5%) against the one-time 2025 sale of commercial hog inventories tied to the Murphy Family Farms/VisionAg formation.
Packaged Meats cost of sales rose $116M on higher raw-material costs and volume; Hog Production cost of sales fell $164M on the same one-time 2025 comparison base.
Decomposes to sales +$29M and cost of sales +$28M, netting to roughly flat gross-profit dollars; margin was essentially unchanged as segment mix shifts offset each other.

SG&A fell $17M (-8.6%) on continued cost-reduction discipline, partly offset by a $4M increase in marketing spend; the 2025 quarter also included a $6M workforce-reduction charge not repeated in 2026.
Lower SG&A and smaller net operating losses (-$1M vs -$9M) drove the $11M increase, as gross profit dollars were roughly flat.

Reconciling items were smaller than a year ago (incremental costs from a sow-farm fire in Laverne, Oklahoma vs 2025 insurance recoveries), so adjusted growth (+4.0%) tracked closely with GAAP growth (+3.4%).

Higher operating profit plus a lower effective tax rate (22.2% vs 23.6%, on smaller interest-accrual adjustments for unrecognized tax benefits) and a smaller equity-method investment loss drove the increase.
Tracks the adjusted operating profit increase plus flat depreciation and amortization ($83M both periods); adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 11.0% from 10.5%.
Tracks the net income increase; diluted weighted-average shares rose modestly (394.7M vs 389.1M) on 2025 stock option/RSU grants, which is why EPS growth (+8.8%) trailed net income growth (+10.0%).
Follows the adjusted net income increase to $251M from $227M, on the same non-GAAP add-backs described for adjusted operating profit.
Not explained item-by-item in the release; consistent with the $101M y/y narrowing of the operating cash outflow against $88M of capex and the absence of 2025's $236M one-time IPO proceeds.

drivers.explanation: Improvement was primarily driven by changes in working capital and higher earnings, including a smaller y/y increase in accounts receivable and a smaller y/y decrease in accrued expenses and other current liabilities.

CEO Shane Smith called it a record first quarter driven by Packaged Meats strength and the vertically integrated model, and the company reaffirmed its FY2026 outlook while continuing to pursue the pending Nathan's Famous acquisition.
